hook: Born in 1860, Phoebe Ann Moses rose from poverty and abuse to conquer the world!

sections.voiceover: Born in 1860, Phoebe Ann Moses rose from poverty and abuse to conquer the world!
sections.visual_cue: Historical portrait photograph of Annie Oakley holding a rifle

sections.voiceover: On August 13, 1860, Phoebe Ann Moses was born in rural Darke County, Ohio. At 15, she defeated marksman Frank E. Butler in a legendary shooting match.
sections.visual_cue: Archival document showing birth records and early shooting targets

sections.voiceover: In 1885, she joined Buffalo Bill's Wild West show and met an iconic leader.
sections.visual_cue: Vintage poster of Buffalo Bill's Wild West
b_roll: Buffalo Bill Wild West show poster

sections.voiceover: Sitting Bull gave her the Lakota name Watanya Cicilia, meaning Little Sure Shot. One hundred years after her 1926 death in Greenville, her marksmanship remains legendary.
sections.visual_cue: Historical photograph of Annie Oakley alongside Sitting Bull
b_roll: Sitting Bull and Annie Oakley photograph

sections.voiceover: Visit Greenville's memorial honoring Annie Oakley's 100-year legacy.
sections.visual_cue: Historic plaque commemorating Annie Oakley in Greenville
